title: Metsähallitus ends counter service at four Lapland visitor centres
seoTitle: Lapland visitor centres lose Metsähallitus service
description: Metsähallitus ended its own customer service at Kellokas, Hetta, Siida and Naava on 11 November 2026. What is still open, and where to get permits now.
dek: The buildings are not all closing. Kellokas in Äkäslompolo has been sold for 730,000 euros, and at Pyhätunturi the restaurant and the exhibition are still open.
heroAlt: A nature centre service desk with a Metsähallitus sign on the wall above it, a leaflet rack, screens on the counter and empty chairs around a low table.
heroCaption: The Metsähallitus service point inside Siida in Inari in October 2026. Its own customer service there ended on 11 November.

body.text: Metsähallitus closed its own customer service at four places in Lapland on 11 November 2026: the Kellokas visitor centre in Äkäslompolo, the Fell Lapland Visitor Centre in Hetta, the Inari service point inside Siida, and the Naava visitor centre at Pyhätunturi. A hiker who walks in now finds no member of staff behind the counter to advise on routes, permits or conditions.

items: Kellokas, Äkäslompolo: the building has been sold, and the new owners take over the running of it in February 2027.
Fell Lapland Visitor Centre, Hetta: the customer service produced by Metsähallitus has ended.
Inari service point: the Sámi Museum Siida continues in the same building.
Naava, Pyhätunturi: the restaurant stays open and the exhibition can still be seen.

body.text: The houses are not all going dark

Metsähallitus is trying by every means to avoid the buildings closing altogether, says Samuli Sillman, deputy director of Metsähallitus Parks and Wildlife Finland. The aim is to find a good operator to carry on the life of each house. Sales are under way for Syöte and for Naava, and Syöte is shut at the moment while those talks continue.

The Yllästunturi visitor centre Kellokas changed hands in the same week. Markus Heikkilä from Muonio and Mikko Saari from Espoo paid 730,000 euros for a package that covers a plot of more than a hectare, the visitor centre building, an accommodation and maintenance building, the log house that served as the Savotta museum, and storage space. The centre will carry on in the local community, Sillman says, but the exhibition will be taken down and moved into digital form. Metsähallitus stays on as a tenant in some of the rooms, and the new owners have said they want to rent space to other businesses as well.
Where to get maps, permits and trail advice now

Metsähallitus has merged its two customer service teams into a single national team that handles digital customer service. The agency says the shrinking network of visitor centres has cut the amount of work tied to counters and exhibitions, while the Luontoon.fi service has been built up and visitors increasingly find what they need for a hike on their own online.

Fishing permits, the fisheries management fee and snowmobile track permits are sold in the Eräluvat.fi service and through the Eräluvat phone service on +358 20 69 2424, which answers on weekdays. Hunting permits are available the same two ways. Local partners also sell the fisheries management fee and track permits, and they add a service fee of 3 euros.

In Inari the Sámi Museum Siida keeps its own doors open through the winter from Monday to Saturday, with an adult ticket at 18 euros and free entry for children under seven. Its main exhibition, which links Sámi culture and northern nature, was produced together with Metsähallitus.
Ten jobs end, a million euros a year saved

The change negotiations held in October and November end the employment of 10 people and alter the essential terms of another 10. Metsähallitus expects permanent annual savings of about one million euros from the decisions. Parks and Wildlife Finland has to cut its costs by about five million euros by 2030, and the savings now agreed are one part of that. The decisions continue a plan made in 2025 to give up the visitor centre network in stages and move the weight of customer service to national digital services.
What else changes around the country

Oulanka visitor centre and the Savukoski service point, which were open in the summer of 2026, will not be run again. At the Haltia and Koli nature centres the customer service produced by a contract partner carries on, and at Haltia the marketing work and part of the technical upkeep of the exhibitions are being bought in from outside.

Metsähallitus had already ended its own customer service at Liminganlahti, Kilpisjärvi, Hossa in Suomussalmi, Syöte in Pudasjärvi, Petola in Kuhmo, Seitseminen in Ylöjärvi and Teijo in Salo, mostly after it gave up owning the buildings. Liminganlahti was bought by the municipality of Liminka, which agreed to keep showing the exhibitions put together by Parks and Wildlife Finland. Moving the Teijo building outside the national park was approved by the government in the same week, which makes that house easier to sell.
Work out your route and your permits before you set off, now that nobody is handing out advice at the counter in Äkäslompolo, Hetta, Inari or Pyhätunturi.
